result.note: Tests the outcomes of the February 2026 AI Impact Summit: the voluntary Charter, the Global AI Impact Commons, open-source emphasis and the guiding philosophy.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the New Delhi Declaration adopted at the close of the AI Impact Summit in February 2026:
items: Its centrepiece is a Charter for the Democratic Diffusion of AI that is binding on all signatory countries.
It proposes a Global AI Impact Commons, a repository to help countries replicate successful AI use cases across borders.
It champions open-source AI as an engine of economic and social development.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The Charter for the Democratic Diffusion of AI is voluntary, not binding, so statement 1 is wrong. The voluntary Global AI Impact Commons and the push for open-source AI are both part of the Declaration, which aims to make AI adoption benefit the Global South.
questions.source: The centerpiece is a voluntary Charter for the Democratic Diffusion of AI.

questions.prompt: The New Delhi Declaration, adopted at the AI Impact Summit in February 2026, invoked which philosophy meaning "the world is one family"?
questions.explain: The Declaration invoked Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, the "world is one family" philosophy. In that spirit, it framed meaningful and affordable connectivity as a necessity for deploying AI rather than a luxury.
questions.source: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam: Invoking the “world is one family” philosophy, the Declaration frames
